pages.text: Now and then, a strange light appears in the evening sky: a fuzzy star with a long, pale tail. It is a comet. In October 2024, one was bright enough to see without a telescope. A comet is a lump of ice, dust, and rock a few kilometres across, left over from the time the planets formed. Most comets stay in the cold outer Solar System. When one comes close to the Sun, its ice turns to gas. The gas and dust stream out into a tail millions of kilometres long, which always points away from the Sun.

pages.text: For most of history, comets frightened people. They appeared without warning and seemed to announce wars or the deaths of kings. Then scientists began to measure them. Around 1700, the English astronomer Edmond Halley noticed that bright comets seen in 1531, 1607, and 1682 had followed the same path. He decided they were one comet returning about every 76 years, and he predicted it would come back in 1758. It did, after his death. Halley’s Comet was last seen in 1986 and will return in 2061. Once people understood gravity, comets became predictable.

pages.alt: An astronomer of the 1700s at a desk with a telescope and star charts, tracing a long curved path across a map of the sky.

pages.text: Earth’s orbit is almost a circle, so its speed hardly changes. A comet’s orbit is a long, stretched oval called an ellipse. Far from the Sun, the comet moves slowly. As the Sun’s gravity pulls it inward, it speeds up, just as a mango falling from a tree speeds up. Its gravitational potential energy is changing into kinetic energy. It whips round the Sun at its fastest. Then, as it climbs away, it slows down, like a ball thrown upward. Kinetic energy is changing back into potential energy. The total energy stays the same throughout.

pages.text: Comets and asteroids sometimes cross the Earth’s path. Small pieces burn up in the air as shooting stars. A large one is a different matter. About 66 million years ago, an asteroid about 10 kilometres wide struck what is now Mexico. Its enormous kinetic energy was changed into heat, light, sound, and shock waves in seconds. Dust and smoke darkened the sky for years, plants died, and most kinds of dinosaur disappeared. Yet space objects may also have helped life. Many scientists think that asteroids and comets delivered some of the water in Earth’s oceans.

pages.text: Ghana has its own scar from space. About one million years ago, a large meteorite struck the forest 30 kilometres south-east of where Kumasi now stands. It blasted out a crater about 10 kilometres across. Rain slowly filled it, forming Lake Bosumtwi, the only natural lake in Ghana. The impact melted rock and flung glassy droplets as far as Côte d’Ivoire, where they are still found today. For years people wondered whether the lake was an old volcano. Studies of the rocks proved that it is an impact crater, one of the best preserved in the world.

pages.text: Could a large impact happen again? It is possible, but very unlikely in our lifetimes. Astronomers now search the sky every night and track thousands of asteroids and comets whose paths come near Earth. None of the large ones they have found is expected to hit us in the next hundred years. We have even begun to practise defending ourselves. In 2022, a spacecraft called DART was deliberately crashed into a small asteroid. The collision changed the asteroid’s orbit slightly. For the first time, people had changed the path of an object in space.

activities.question: Why does a comet grow a tail when it comes near the Sun?
options: It catches fire in the Earth’s atmosphere
The Sun’s heat turns its ice into gas, which streams away with dust

activities.question: Where in its orbit does a comet move fastest?
options: When it is farthest from the Sun
When it is closest to the Sun

activities.question: How was Lake Bosumtwi formed?
options: By a volcano that erupted and then collapsed
By a dam built across a river
By a meteorite that struck the Earth and left a crater

activities.question: Apply it: A child on a swing is highest at each end and fastest at the bottom. Which statement matches the comet’s orbit?
options: The ends of the swing are like the comet close to the Sun
The bottom of the swing, where speed is greatest, is like being near the Sun
The swing has no potential energy at any point

activities.prompt: Arrange from earliest to most recent.
items: An asteroid strikes Mexico and most dinosaurs die out (66 million years ago)
A meteorite forms the Bosumtwi crater (about 1 million years ago)
Halley’s Comet is last seen from Earth (1986)
The DART spacecraft changes an asteroid’s orbit (2022)

Kinetic energy: the energy an object has because it is moving.
A rocky object, smaller than a planet, that orbits the Sun.
